claims.text: Nanoscale chemical and structural heterogeneities enhance the magnetocaloric effect of rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys at low applied fields.
Locally segregated regions foster strong magnetoelastic coupling.
Nanoscale chemical and structural heterogeneities are intrinsic to high-entropy alloy designs.
Heterogeneities promote a sharp second-order magnetic transition near the Curie temperature.
Rare-earth-free Fe-Zr-B-Cu-based alloys can exhibit a second-order paramagnetic-to-ferromagnetic transition near room temperature.
Rare-earth-free Mn-Fe-Ni-based compositionally complex alloys exhibit ferromagnetic-to-paramagnetic transitions at their Curie temperatures.
The heterogeneous microstructure maintains rapid phonon transport.
The heterogeneous microstructure produces low magnetic-domain-wall pinning.
Rapid phonon transport and low domain-wall pinning provide rapid heat exchange and low hysteresis.
The proposed heterogeneous microstructure maintains mechanical stability.
The as-cast rare-earth-free high-entropy-alloy baseline inherently contains nanoscale heterogeneities.
Prolonged annealing followed by slow cooling reduces nanoscale inhomogeneity and homogenizes the microstructure.
Rapid quenching preserves the proposed nanoscale heterogeneities.
Heterogeneous regions act as nucleation sites for the magnetic transition and thereby increase magnetic entropy change at low fields.
Interconnected heterogeneous regions facilitate rapid heat transfer.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, prolonged annealing will reduce magnetic entropy change.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, prolonged annealing will increase magnetic hysteresis.
Homogenization will diminish heat-exchange performance by reducing efficient phonon-transport pathways.
The proposed mechanism should apply near the Curie temperature and at applied fields up to approximately 2 T.
